title: kioku.tool.v1 error registry
description: The whole frozen wire vocabulary, with the response status each name resolves to, whether a caller may retry, and the HTTP status the Rails surface answers with. Both deploy units read this table; neither keeps its own copy. A name outside it cannot reach a caller, so an invented condition cannot arrive under a plausible-looking name.
x-kioku-http-note: http_status is an interpretation, not contract text: contracts.json names no HTTP mapping. It binds the Rails surface only. The host branches on code and status and ignores it, so a change here can never change what the model is told.

ok.condition: the request was fully satisfied within scope, budget and deadline
ok.note: error is null. Coverage may still be partial in the evidence sense without changing status; coverage.state carries that, not status.

kioku.partial_result.condition: an authorized, in-budget answer was produced but some declared portion could not be served
kioku.partial_result.note: data present, coverage.state=partial, gaps enumerated. Retrying produces the same partial result; the caller continues with a cursor instead. Applicability filtering that removes results triggers a bounded refill first; material contrary evidence is never the thing dropped to fit.

kioku.queued.condition: the write was durably enqueued on the host spool but has not reached canonical commit
kioku.queued.note: Carries {spool_entry_id, producer_key, producer_epoch, producer_sequence, saved:false}. retryable is true because retrying is the contract's own mechanism: 'Replay after reconnect returns the same idempotency receipt.' Re-issuing with the same idempotency key and request digest is how the caller learns the commit outcome, exactly as for kioku.deadline_exceeded. Resolves D5.

kioku.revision_conflict.condition: expected_revision is stale or the target head moved
kioku.revision_conflict.note: details carries {current_revision, current_head, target_key}. The stale writer fails; nothing is written.

kioku.idempotency_conflict.condition: the supplied idempotency key was reused, within the same actor scope, with a different request digest
kioku.idempotency_conflict.note: Nothing is written. details carries the prior receipt id and the differing digest. The lookup is (actor_principal_id, idempotency_key): a second actor reusing a key never sees the first actor's receipt id or digest, because it never matches their receipt.

kioku.authority_violation.condition: an authority-changing edit was attempted without the backing authority
kioku.authority_violation.note: The objection or proposal is preserved as an auditable record where the document requires it; the authority transition is refused. An assistant's objection cannot cancel a governing user constraint.

kioku.evidence_required.condition: an explicit memory write supplied no ELIGIBLE evidence link
kioku.evidence_required.note: Raised when the eligible set is empty after per-entry evaluation, not when a single ref is unresolvable. A well-formed but unresolvable ref is reported in data.evidence_rejected with a named reason. Resolves half of D4.

kioku.continuation_expired.condition: a continuation cursor expired, or its bound scope/query/generation digest no longer matches
kioku.continuation_expired.note: details carries reset_required_reason. The caller restarts the query; no permanent score ordering is promised.

kioku.precondition_failed.condition: context_task close was attempted against a receipt that is no longer applicable, or heads moved since the caller observed them
kioku.precondition_failed.note: details enumerates the concrete mismatch: {stale_heads, receipt_state, invalidating_changes}. Returns the mismatch, never a partial close.

kioku.scope_denied.condition: the requested project/global/cross-project scope is not granted to the authenticated principal
kioku.scope_denied.note: data absent. Denial is uniform across fetch, caches, graph traversal, facets and aggregates and must not disclose whether the target exists in another scope.

http_status_override.reason: The contract freezes no separate authentication code, so an unrecognised credential is denied with this code but answered 401: the credential, not the requested scope, is what failed. The denial still discloses nothing about what exists.

kioku.project_binding_unresolved.condition: the project binding is missing or ambiguous for a project-scoped request
kioku.project_binding_unresolved.note: details.setup_required=true. The core surfaces setup state; it never attaches another project's history and never reinterprets unresolved project capture as global.

kioku.handle_unresolved.condition: a handle did not resolve, whether because it does not exist or because it belongs to a scope the caller cannot see
kioku.handle_unresolved.note: Deliberately merged so not-found and wrong-scope are indistinguishable; the internal audit log distinguishes them. The status is unauthorized_scope because the caller's branch is the same in both cases ('this is not obtainable') and because giving it a status of its own would reintroduce nothing useful. Both merged branches answer 404, so the HTTP status distinguishes nothing either. Resolves part of D1.

kioku.source_unavailable.condition: the host control connection is down, or the caller set require_source_validation and a selected dependency could not be checked before the deadline
kioku.source_unavailable.note: This is NOT the default behavior. By default the request succeeds with applicability historical or unknown and a host_disconnected coverage gap. Returned only when the caller demanded validation. Late validation responses cannot satisfy a newer request or source epoch.

kioku.evidence_unavailable.condition: the referenced revision, object or evidence handle was privacy-deleted, tombstoned, purged, redacted, or its retention expired
kioku.evidence_unavailable.note: details.reason in (deleted|expired|purged|redacted). Deletion epochs prevent queued jobs and replays from resurrecting it. In batch reads this appears per item in data.unavailable[] and the request status becomes partial.

kioku.quota_exhausted.note: details {quota_kind, limit, observed, retry_after_ms}. Disk or spool exhaustion produces visible failure and loss accounting; it never produces a false durable acknowledgment.

kioku.deadline_exceeded.condition: the bounded deadline_ms elapsed before a result could be produced
kioku.deadline_exceeded.note: For reads, nothing is returned rather than an unlabeled fragment. For writes the outcome is indeterminate by design: the caller retries with the same idempotency key and request digest, which returns the prior receipt if the commit landed. A deadline expiry is never reported as a save.

kioku.invalid_request.condition: the request failed schema, enum, bound, cardinality, digest or closure validation, or supplied a core-derived field
kioku.invalid_request.note: status 'invalid' is the tenth value contracts.json proposed for v1.1, taken in v1 instead. The previous reading omitted status entirely, which made a client branch on two fields and made this code indistinguishable at the status level from a core fault. Resolves D1.

kioku.unsupported_schema_version.condition: the request declared an unsupported schema_version MAJOR
kioku.unsupported_schema_version.note: Returned before any scope resolution, so generation_vector is null on this response and only on this one and a malformed envelope. A minor this build does not implement is NOT this error: the version is accepted and any unknown field is refused by the closure rule instead. Resolves D2.

kioku.unsupported_operation.condition: an operation, enum value or contract-named input is not supported by this contract version or by this build
kioku.unsupported_operation.note: Covers an unknown context_task op, an unvalidated edge kind, mode=semantic or mode=hybrid (permanently unsupported, embeddings are out of scope), hops greater than 2, and a contract-named property this build has not implemented, which carries details.reason='not_implemented_in_this_build'.

kioku.internal_error.note: No partial write is implied. Services do not swallow unexpected exceptions or turn failed saves into successful results. message is content- and credential-redacted; the raised text stays on the server log and never reaches the wire. 'internal_error' is a status value of its own because mapping a core fault onto any caller-fault value reports a 500 as a client error, which is the observed defect. Resolves D1.
